caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: This plot illustrates the accuracy of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes the LLM without editing. The x-axis represents Co-occurrence Number on a logarithmic scale, ranging from approximately 3 to beyond 10³, with tick marks at 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis represents ACC (%), on a linear scale ranging from approximately 37% to 65%, with gridlines and tick marks at intervals of 5 percentage points. Six data series are shown, each as a line with distinct color and marker. The Base line (black with circle markers, solid) starts at approximately 37% at the lowest co-occurrence number, rises to about 43.5% around co-occurrence number 30, then plateaus near 43.5–44% for the remaining range. The FT line (light blue with downward-pointing triangle markers, solid) begins at approximately 39.5%, increases steadily, and reaches about 47.5% at the highest co-occurrence number. The IKE line (red with upward-pointing triangle markers, solid) starts at approximately 43%, rises to about 44.5% at co-occurrence number 30, continues to approximately 46% around 300, and reaches roughly 49% at the highest value. The MEND line (brown with diamond markers, solid) begins at approximately 44.5%, increases to about 48.5% at co-occurrence number 30, rises further to approximately 54% around 300, and reaches roughly 56.5% at the highest co-occurrence number. The MEMIT line (purple with pentagon markers, solid) starts at approximately 43.5%, increases to about 51% at co-occurrence number 30, rises to approximately 53% around 300, and reaches roughly 55% at the highest value. The ROME line (green with square markers, solid) begins at approximately 51%, increases to about 57% at co-occurrence number 30, rises to approximately 62% around 300, and reaches roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence number. All six lines show a general upward trend with increasing co-occurrence number, with ROME consistently achieving the highest accuracy values across the entire range and Base consistently the lowest.
